## Policies

### liminalkit is an explicit-state, software-rendered toolkit; abstractions stay visible and optional

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.policy.explicit-state-toolkit/1` · scope `all` · topic `positioning`

liminalkit is positioned as a lightweight GUI toolkit for applications that need direct control over drawing, interaction and resource use: desktop utilities, operational interfaces, kiosks and embedded Linux displays. Caller-owned state, immediate-mode controls and software rendering, with no browser, no retained widget tree, no widget identity map and no mandatory GPU stack. Every new subsystem must make its ownership, allocations and any state kept between frames visible in its signature; a hidden mechanism that undermines predictability needs a strong, recorded justification. Layout helpers are stateless functions from a rectangle to rectangles; a retained layout hierarchy is not added without an overwhelming reason. The toolkit does not aim at feature parity with egui, Dioxus or Freya, and does not try to become a universal application framework.
